entities.name: PMID:25087999
observations: Xu et al. studied 514 Chinese males aged 22–79 years selected for normal BMI and normal liver enzymes.
Serum 25(OH)D3 was measured by electrochemiluminescence immunoassay; NAFLD was assessed by abdominal ultrasound and fatty liver index.
The study was observational and does not establish causality.

entities.name: 25-hydroxyvitamin D3
observations: Serum 25(OH)D3 was lower in NAFLD than non-NAFLD participants: 13.46±4.65 vs 15.65±5.89 ng/mL, P=0.002.
Serum 25(OH)D3 was inversely associated with fatty liver index after age and BMI adjustment (r=-0.108, P=0.014).

entities.name: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
observations: Among 514 normal-weight Chinese males with normal liver enzymes, 76 had ultrasound-diagnosed NAFLD.
Logistic regression showed an inverse association between serum 25(OH)D3 and NAFLD: OR 0.937 per ng/mL increase, 95% CI 0.884–0.993, P=0.028.
The evidence supports an inverse observational association but is limited to one clearly eligible study and may be affected by residual confounding or reverse causation.
